title: Tuscaloosa and Birmingham, April 27, 2011
summary: Follow one documented tornado through three retained county records, contrasting damage, warning communication and source definitions. No geographic replay or registered appearance is claimed.

records.basis: Greene segment narrative names the continuing Tuscaloosa and Birmingham tornado. Continuation targets Tuscaloosa County FIPS 125. Its end matches the Tuscaloosa segment beginning, and its start matches the approximate survey beginning. Reviewed October 5, 2026 against retained continuation, endpoints and original survey text. No source fields merged.

Tuscaloosa segment follows the same named damage progression. Its beginning matches Greene end, continuation targets Jefferson County FIPS 073, and its ending matches Jefferson beginning. Reviewed October 5, 2026 against retained continuation, endpoints and original survey text. No source fields merged.

Jefferson segment continues the same surveyed track from western Jefferson County to northeast of Birmingham. Its beginning matches Tuscaloosa end and its ending matches the approximate survey ending. Reviewed October 5, 2026 against retained continuation, endpoints and original survey text. No source fields merged.

observations.title: A track association across three county records
observations.locator: Event IDs 314625, 314662 and 314663: continuation fields, shared boundary endpoints and opening narratives.
observations.account: Greene continues into Tuscaloosa. Tuscaloosa continues into Jefferson. The corresponding boundary endpoints match. Their narratives describe the same tornado beginning in northern Greene County and crossing Tuscaloosa and the western Birmingham suburbs.
observations.limits: The reviewed association retains all three source IDs and county-specific fields. An episode ID, date or proximity alone is not the association basis. Source endpoints do not produce a surveyed route or historical appearance.

observations.title: Violent damage and differing building outcomes in Jefferson County
observations.locator: Written account from Concord and Pleasant Grove through McDonald Chapel, Smithfield Estates, Interstate 65 and U.S. 31.
observations.account: The survey identifies EF4 damage at Concord and Pleasant Grove, then EF2 damage at McDonald Chapel and Smithfield Estates. At McDonald Chapel it contrasts severely damaged pier-and-beam homes with a brick home that lost its roof. Near Interstate 65 it reports the track maximum width.
observations.limits: This is one survey/reporting stream and an attributed damage interpretation. Building outcomes alone do not isolate exposure, construction, debris impact or failure sequence. No wind field or victim location is inferred.

observations.title: Damage width and inferred wind remain distinct from appearance
observations.locator: Summary rating, estimated maximum wind and maximum width. McDonald Chapel contrast. Interstate 65 account.
observations.account: The survey's whole-track rating is EF4, estimated maximum wind is 190 mph, and maximum reported width is 2,600 yards near Interstate 65. Its written damage descriptions distinguish local outcomes along the track.
observations.limits: The wind estimate is damage-based, not a sensor reading at every home. A damage width is not condensation-funnel diameter and does not establish time-varying optical appearance. Visual similarity is not a measurement.

observations.title: Two storms and the challenge of managing one warning area
observations.locator: Printed pages 17 and 18 (PDF 25 and 26): Warngen findings and Tuscaloosa warning examples.
observations.account: The assessment describes a warning issued at 4:15 p.m. CDT for a supercell in western Tuscaloosa County. A new supercell then formed within the polygon, making pathcasts difficult to manage. It separately identifies the named Tuscaloosa landmarks in the warning immediately before the tornado struck as a best practice.
observations.limits: These are distinct source findings, not proof that no warning existed or that Tuscaloosa was omitted from the location list. The report discusses city-name omissions elsewhere. This is a wider outbreak review. No local warning lead time is calculated from an outbreak-wide average.

place.basis: Source description. no warning polygon acquired or registered.

observations.review: Selected original report text inspected. No source figure pixels or new warning geometry inspected.

observations.title: Receiving a warning and reaching shelter were separate questions
observations.locator: Printed pages 29 and 30 (PDF 37 and 38), 35 to 37 (PDF 43 to 45), Appendix C (PDF 60 and 61).
observations.account: The report describes police using bullhorns along Tuscaloosa streets, disrupted power and communication, and limited shelter availability. Survivor interviews across affected states were conducted 10 to 13 days after the outbreak.
observations.limits: The sample was not random or representative, excluded hospital interviews with severely injured people and direct interviews with deceased victims' families, and did not use a structured questionnaire. Its themes are not population percentages or proof of every resident action.

observations.title: Different reported totals and direct/indirect classifications
observations.locator: Event IDs 314625, 314662 and 314663 impacts and narrative. compare NWS survey summary and assessment Table 1, printed page 6 (PDF 14).
observations.account: The survey page lists 65 fatalities. The December 2011 assessment summary lists 66 for Tuscaloosa and Jefferson. The retained 2026 NCEI revision reports 44 direct and 8 indirect deaths in Tuscaloosa, 20 direct and 0 indirect in Jefferson, and none in Greene. The Tuscaloosa narrative includes deaths reported in the months afterward.
observations.limits: Attribution, revision, county scope and direct/indirect definitions remain separate. No canonical summed total or reason for every difference is established. No names, deaths or recovery locations are mapped from these counts.

observations.title: Source clock conventions and differing summary scope
observations.locator: Three segment begin/end clock fields. NWS survey approximate times. assessment Table 1, printed page 6 (PDF 14).
observations.account: The retained segments report 15:43 to 15:48, 15:48 to 16:35, and 16:35 to 17:14 under CST-6. The importer retains standard-time labels and converts the combined interval to 21:43 through 23:14 UTC. The survey reports approximate 4:43 to 6:14 p.m. CDT. Assessment Table 1 labels Time (CST) and reports 3:50 to 4:45 p.m. for Tuscaloosa and Jefferson.
observations.limits: Standard-time conversion explains the one-hour clock-label difference at matching survey endpoints. It does not reconcile the assessment's shorter interval, register a camera or establish each place's arrival minute. No synchronized playback or position interpolation is supplied.
